title: The Brahmin of Kasur Appeals to the Khalsa

blocks.text: The new Kasur episode begins with ordinary Khalsa discipline at Amritsar before a crisis interrupts it. There arrived a Brahmin from the city of Kasur, and he appears not as a court envoy but as a distressed petitioner demanding public justice from the Panth.

His complaint is direct and urgent: his spouse had been abducted by Kasur Pathans, and he frames the outrage as a test of Khalsa responsibility toward vulnerable Hindus. The appeal presses on the old claim that the Khalsa having been created for the protection of the Hindus cannot ignore such tyranny without dishonor.

The page closes with the matter moving from lament into formal hearing. Hari Singh instructs the Brahmin to present the grievance before the assembled congregation after the evening prayer so the case can be taken up in the proper collective setting.
